What the catalogue knows about a glyph

Source: R/emoji-catalogue.R
emoji_properties.Rd

emoji_properties() reports, for each glyph, everything the bundled emoji catalogue records about it: its code points, its qualification status, its Unicode name, group and subgroup, the emoji version that introduced it, and whether it can carry a skin-tone modifier. With no argument it returns the whole catalogue, one row per spelling.

Usage

emoji_properties(x = NULL)

Arguments

x

A character vector of glyphs. The default, NULL, returns every spelling in the catalogue, in the catalogue's own order.

Value

A tibble with one row per element of x (or per catalogue spelling), in the same order, and columns emoji, codepoints (as "U+1F600 U+FE0F"), n_codepoints, key (the code-point key, with U+FE0F removed), name, status, group, subgroup, version (the emoji version that introduced it, such as "15.0"), modifiable and has_fe0f.

Details

The catalogue is Unicode's emoji-test.txt for the version emoji_unicode_version() reports. It lists every spelling of every emoji, and status is what the file calls the spelling:

  • "fully-qualified": the spelling a keyboard emits, carrying every U+FE0F the emoji needs. Exactly one per emoji.

  • "minimally-qualified": a shorter spelling of a joined sequence, with some selectors left out but the first one kept.

  • "unqualified": a spelling with the first selector left out too, such as the bare heart U+2764. These are detected only under presentation = "any"; see emoji_summary().

  • "component": the five skin-tone swatches and four hair components, which are parts of emoji rather than emoji. Standing alone they are not counted by any verb.

status describes the exact spelling you passed, so it is NA for one the catalogue does not list: a correct emoji with a stray extra U+FE0F, a sequence too new for this catalogue, or a string that is not an emoji at all. The other catalogue columns describe the emoji, and are looked up through the code-point key every verb uses, which ignores U+FE0F: the bare and the qualified heart share a name, a group and a version. The codepoints, n_codepoints and has_fe0f columns describe the string itself and are filled in for anything, emoji or not.

modifiable is TRUE when the catalogue spells the emoji with a skin tone, so it is a statement about the emoji with any tone it carries removed: U+1F44D and U+1F44D U+1F3FD are both modifiable. It is NA where the emoji is not in the catalogue.

See also

as_emoji_canonical() for the fully-qualified spelling, emoji_identical() to compare two glyphs, emoji_unicode_releases() to turn version into a date, and emoji_keywords() for the vocabulary.

Examples

emoji_properties(c("\u2764", "\u2764\ufe0f", "\U0001f44d\U0001f3fd"))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 11
#>   emoji codepoints      n_codepoints key     name  status group subgroup version
#>   <chr> <chr>                  <int> <chr>   <chr> <chr>  <chr> <chr>    <chr>  
#> 1 ❤     U+2764                     1 2764    red … unqua… Smil… heart    0.6    
#> 2 ❤️     U+2764 U+FE0F              2 2764    red … fully… Smil… heart    0.6    
#> 3 👍🏽    U+1F44D U+1F3FD            2 1F44D … thum… fully… Peop… hand-fi… 1.0    
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: modifiable <lgl>, has_fe0f <lgl>

# the whole catalogue, one row per spelling
cat <- emoji_properties()
table(cat$status)
#> 
#>           component     fully-qualified minimally-qualified         unqualified 
#>                   9                3963                1029                 243
